newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks dip at open, News Corp dives.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks dip at open, News Corp dives.

text.p: Australian shares sagged at the open on Tuesday with media giant News Corp leading the way down as traders expressed disappointment at a spending spree by media baron Rupert Murdoch.
Papua New Guinea-linked stocks, which fell sharply on Monday after the nation's army chief called for the resignation of the prime minister, recovered some ground.
The All Ordinaries index lost 13.1 points to 2,414.3.

Brokers said while News Corp's US$1.35 billion purchase of U.S. television and radio owner Heritage Media Corp may prove of strategic value and boost earnings down the track, initial reaction had been negative because of the dilutive effect of the seemingly continous issue of new shares for new acquistions.
"Some reports have the deal as earnings-positive but issuing more shares just dilutes everyone," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
"People are not happy he is still spending."
News Corp shares slid 3.7 percent to A$6.34 (US$5.01).

PNG stocks dipped early although they seemed to find a base with several moving back to square or even adding a few cents. Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan confirmed on Tuesday he had sacked defence force chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok.
"They still have to settle issues up there but they have been a bit better behaved today," the dealer said.

Orogen Minerals dived 22 cents to an intraday low of A$2.98 before recouping some losses to be seven cents lower at A$3.13. Oilsearch and Lihir Gold also headed south in initial trade before rebounding off their lows and making their way back towards square. Oilsearch shares were five cents up at A$2.65, while Lihir shares were up four cents at A$2.14.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about two to one, while about 46 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
